motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.17 Appointed Officers, and Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.27 Board Appointment Process. Ms. Kofoed reviewed the item as presented during work session. She read the email Councilmember Curtis sent to the Council that was mentioned during work session with his suggested changes to the amendment. The Council discussed the proposed amendment and determined to approve the following changes: • EMMC 2.17.010 Process for Appointing Officers – In accordance with Utah Code Ann. § 10-3-9, the mayor, with the advice and consent of the city council, shall appoint a qualified person to the office of city recorder, city treasurer, city attorney and city engineer. If Eagle Mountain City creates a municipal fire or police department, the police chief and fire chief shall also be appointed officers. All appointed officers shall continue in office until their successors are appointed and qualified. All appointments of officers designated herein shall follow the process as outlined in EMMC 2.27 Appointment Process. • EMMC Chapter 2.27 Appointment Process: o 2.27.010 Definitions - “Statutorily appointed” shall mean any position designated in EMMC 2.17.010 Appointed Officers. o 2.27.020 Appointment – Unless otherwise designated, the mayor shall appoint all advisory board members, statutorily appointed officers, and planning commission members with the advice and consent of the city council. o 2.27.030 Posting of Positions – Notice of all empty or expiring advisory board, statutorily appointed positions, or planning commission members shall be posted on the city webpage, or other method suitable to provide notice to the public, for a minimum of ten days. The notice shall include a description of the position and provide details for the submission of an application or resume for the position. The mayor shall compile and evaluate all applications or resumes for the position. o 2.27.040 Notice to Council – Not less than three (3) days prior to publicly noticing the possible appointment or reappointment of any person to an advisory board, planning commission, or statutorily appointed position, the mayor shall provide to each member of the city council the name, and application or resume if available, of each person the mayor is considering appointing to an advisory board, planning commission, or statutorily appointed position. Members of the city council may individually provide the mayor with feedback or recommendations regarding each potential appointment. o 2.27.050 Removal – An advisory board or planning commission member may be removed with or without cause by the mayor with the advice and consent of the city council.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.17 Appointed Officers, and amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.27 Board Appointment Process as discussed and read by Councilmember Curtis. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
